finding_text: Your firm is registered as a human drug manufacturer. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) conducted testing of consumer antiseptic rub drug product (also referred to as a consumer hand sanitizer), labeled as NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution. This drug product was labeled as manufactured at your facility, Rodriguez Fierro, Marco Antonio, FEI 3016978072, at Avenida Las Americas 409, Col. Leon Xiii, Guadalupe, Nuevo Leon 67120, Mexico. Following an attempt to import NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution into the United States, it was detained and refused admission at the border. The results of the FDA laboratory testing of a batch of this product detained at the border demonstrate that this drug product labeled as manufactured at your facility is adulterated within the meaning of section 501(c) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act or Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(c), in that its strength, purity, or quality falls below that which it purports or is represented to possess. In addition, this product is adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)), in that the subpotency demonstrates that the quality assurance within your facility is not functioning in accordance with Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) requirements. In addition, NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution is an unapproved new drug introduced or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce in violation of section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355(a), and is misbranded under sections 502(a) and (ee) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(a) and (ee). Introduction or delivery for introduction of such a product into interstate commerce is prohibited under sections 301(d) and (a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d) and (a). These violations are described in more detail below. Adulteration Violations NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution, labeled as manufactured at your facility, is labeled to contain 75% volume/volume (v/v) of the active ingredient alcohol, ethyl alcohol (ethanol). However, FDA laboratory testing of a batch of this product detained at the border found that the drug product contained only 31% v/v ethanol. This hand sanitizer drug product is adulterated under section 501(c) of the FD&C Act in that the active ingredient of ethanol is present at levels in the product lower than that which is declared on its label. CDC recommends 1 that, if soap and water are not readily available, consumers use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer that contains not less than 60% alcohol (ethanol). This is the minimum active ingredient concentration of ethanol specified in the 1994 Tentative Final Monograph for Health-Care Antiseptic Drug Products (59 FR 31402), as further amended by “Safety and Effectiveness of Consumer Antiseptics; Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Proposed Amendment of the Tentative Final Monograph; Reopening of Administrative Record,” Proposed Rule, 81 FR 42912 (June 30, 2016). While the contaminated drug product detailed above was shipped to the United States, information available to FDA demonstrated that all of your hand sanitizers were detained and refused admission at the border and did not enter the United States. Therefore, FDA did not recommend that you remove this product from the market. On September 17, 2020, FDA notified the public of the subpotency of your hand sanitizer drug products at the following website: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-updates-hand-sanitizers-consumers-should-not-use In response to this letter, provide the following: • A detailed investigation into how the hand sanitizer drug product described above, which was labeled as containing 75% ethanol, in fact contained an average of 31% ethanol, respectively. • A list of all raw materials used to manufacture your hand sanitizer drug products, including the suppliers’ names, addresses, and contact information. • A list of all batches of any hand sanitizer drug products shipped to the United States by your firm, and a full reconciliation of all material you distributed. • Copies of the complete batch records for all batches distributed to the U.S. The subpotency of hand sanitizer drug products labeled as manufactured in your facility demonstrates that the quality assurance within your facility is not functioning in accordance with CGMP requirements under section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Act. 2 Unapproved New Drug and Misbranding Violations NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution is a “drug” as defined by section 201(g)(1)(B) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(B), because it is intended for use in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease and/or under section 201(g)(1)(C) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(C), because it is intended to affect the structure or any function of the body. Specifically, this product is intended as a topical antiseptic. Examples of claims observed on the NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution product label and labeling that provide evidence of the intended use (as defined in 21 CFR 201.128) of the product include, but may not be limited to, the following: “HAND SANITIZER . . .. Drug Facts … Purpose …Antiseptic… Uses : Hand Sanitizer to help reduce bacteria that potentially can cause disease . . . Directions … Place enough product on hands to cover all surface. Rub hands together until dry.” This topical antiseptic product is a “new drug” within the meaning of section 201(p) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(p), because it is not generally recognized as safe and effective (GRASE) for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its labeling. New drugs may not be introduced or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce without prior approval from FDA, as described in section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355(a), unless they are lawfully marketed under Section 505G of the FD&C Act (which is not the case for these products, as further described below). No FDA-approved application pursuant to section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355, is in effect for this hand sanitizer product, nor are we aware of any adequate and well-controlled clinical studies in the published literature that support a determination that your “NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution” drug product is GRASE for use under the conditions suggested, recommended, or prescribed in its labeling. Accordingly, this product is an unapproved new drug marketed in violation of sections 505(a) and 301(d) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C 355(a) and 331(d). We note that over-the-counter (OTC) topical antiseptic products had been the subject of rulemaking under the Agency’s OTC Drug Review. In particular, such products were addressed in a tentative final monograph (TFM) entitled “Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Tentative Final Monograph for Health-Care Antiseptic Drug Products,” Proposed Rule, 59 FR 31402 (June 17, 1994) (1994 TFM), as further amended by “Safety and Effectiveness of Consumer Antiseptics; Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Proposed Amendment of the Tentative Final Monograph; Reopening of Administrative Record,” Proposed Rule, 81 FR 42912 (June 30, 2016) )(Consumer Antiseptic Rubs Proposed Rule). Over the course of these rulemakings, benzalkonium chloride, ethyl alcohol (ethanol), and isopropyl alcohol were classified in Category III for use in antiseptic rubs, meaning that additional safety and effectiveness data are needed to support a determination that a drug product containing one of these active ingredients would be GRASE for use as a consumer or health care personnel antiseptic rub. Section 505G of the FD&C Act addresses nonprescription drugs marketed without an approved application. Under 505G(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, drugs that were classified as Category III for safety or effectiveness in a TFM that is the most recently applicable proposal or determination for such drug issued under 21 CFR Part 330 – and that were not classified as Category II for safety or effectiveness – are not required to have an approved application under section 505 in order to be marketed, as long as they are in conformity with the relevant conditions of use outlined in the applicable TFM, including the active ingredient, and comply with all other applicable requirements. However, your NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution drug product does not conform to the 1994 TFM, as further amended by the 2016 Consumer Antiseptic Rub proposed rule, nor any other TFM or final rule, and do not meet the conditions under section 505G(a)(3) of the FD&C Act for marketing without an approved application under section 505. According to the product label, NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution drug product purportedly contains the active ingredient ethyl alcohol (ethanol) 75% v/v. However, as previously discussed, FDA laboratory analyses of a batch of this product detained at the border demonstrated that NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution contains ethanol in a concentration that is less than the 75% v/v stated on its product label and less than the amount of ethanol described in the 1994 TFM.3 Such a product does not conform with the TFM or the applicable requirements, nor is it consistent with the formulations described in the guidances setting forth FDA’s temporary policies for hand sanitizers during the COVID-19 public health emergency. 4 Additionally, this hand sanitizer is misbranded under section 502(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(a), because its labeling is false or misleading. As noted above, NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution is labeled to contain ethanol 75% v/v. However, FDA laboratory analysis of this product demonstrate that the product contains concentrations of ethanol that are far less than that stated on its product label. Thus, the misleading representations of the concentration of the active ingredient ethanol on the NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution labeling cause this product to be misbranded under section 502(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(a). Lastly, this product is misbranded under section 502(ee) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(ee), because NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution is a nonprescription drug subject to section 505G of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355h, but does not comply with the requirements for marketing under that section and is not the subject of an application approved under section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355. The introduction or delivery for introduction of a misbranded drug into interstate commerce is prohibited under section 301(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(a). CGMP Consultant Recommended Based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, we strongly recommend engaging a consultant qualified, as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34, to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements if your firm intends to resume manufacturing drugs for the U.S. market. We also recommend that the qualified consultant perform a comprehensive audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and that the consultant evaluates the completion and efficacy of your corrective actions and preventive actions before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. Your use of a consultant does not relieve your firm’s obligation to comply with CGMP. Your firm’s executive management remains responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure ongoing CGMP compliance.
finding_text_ko: 귀사는 사람용 의약품 제조업체로 등록되어 있다. 미국 식품의약국(FDA)은 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution으로 표시된 소비자용 손소독제(antiseptic rub, 소비자용 핸드 새니타이저라고도 함) 의약품을 시험했다. 이 의약품은 귀사 시설인 Rodriguez Fierro, Marco Antonio, FEI 3016978072(Avenida Las Americas 409, Col. Leon Xiii, Guadalupe, Nuevo Leon 67120, Mexico)에서 제조된 것으로 표시되어 있었다. NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution을 미국으로 반입하려는 시도 후 이 제품은 국경에서 억류되어 반입이 거부되었다. 국경에서 억류된 이 제품 한 배치에 대한 FDA 실험실 시험 결과는 귀사 시설에서 제조된 것으로 표시된 이 의약품이 함량, 순도 또는 품질이 표방하거나 표시된 것보다 낮다는 점에서 연방식품의약품화장품법(FD&C Act 또는 Act) 섹션 501(c), 21 U.S.C. 351(c)의 의미 내에서 불량의약품(adulterated)임을 보여준다. 또한 이 제품은 함량 미달이 귀사 시설 내 품질보증이 현행 우수제조관리기준(CGMP) 요건에 따라 기능하지 않음을 보여준다는 점에서 FD&C Act 섹션 501(a)(2)(B)(21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B))의 의미 내에서도 불량의약품이다. 아울러 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution은 FD&C Act 섹션 505(a), 21 U.S.C. 355(a)를 위반하여 주 간(interstate) 거래에 반입되거나 반입 목적으로 인도된 미승인 신약이며, FD&C Act 섹션 502(a) 및 (ee), 21 U.S.C. 352(a) 및 (ee)에 따른 허위표시(misbranded) 의약품이다. 이러한 제품을 주 간 거래에 반입하거나 반입 목적으로 인도하는 행위는 FD&C Act 섹션 301(d) 및 (a), 21 U.S.C. 331(d) 및 (a)에 의해 금지된다. 이 위반 사항은 아래에 더 자세히 설명한다. 불량의약품 위반 귀사 시설에서 제조된 것으로 표시된 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution은 유효성분 알코올인 에틸알코올(에탄올)을 75% 부피/부피(v/v) 함유하는 것으로 표시되어 있다. 그러나 국경에서 억류된 이 제품 한 배치에 대한 FDA 실험실 시험에서 이 의약품은 에탄올을 31% v/v만 함유하는 것으로 확인되었다. 이 손소독제 의약품은 유효성분 에탄올이 제품에서 라벨에 표시된 수준보다 낮은 수준으로 존재하므로 FD&C Act 섹션 501(c)에 따라 불량의약품이다. CDC는 비누와 물을 쉽게 쓸 수 없을 때 소비자가 알코올(에탄올)을 60% 이상 함유한 알코올 기반 손소독제를 사용할 것을 권고한다. 1 이는 Health-Care Antiseptic Drug Products에 대한 1994년 Tentative Final Monograph(59 FR 31402)에 명시된 에탄올의 최소 유효성분 농도이며, "Safety and Effectiveness of Consumer Antiseptics; Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Proposed Amendment of the Tentative Final Monograph; Reopening of Administrative Record," Proposed Rule, 81 FR 42912(2016년 6월 30일)에 의해 추가로 개정되었다. 위에서 상술한 오염된 의약품이 미국으로 선적되었으나, FDA가 입수한 정보에 따르면 귀사의 모든 손소독제는 국경에서 억류되어 반입이 거부되었으며 미국에 들어오지 않았다. 따라서 FDA는 귀사에 이 제품을 시장에서 회수하라고 권고하지 않았다. 2020년 9월 17일 FDA는 다음 웹사이트에서 귀사 손소독제 의약품의 함량 미달을 대중에 알렸다. https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-updates-hand-sanitizers-consumers-should-not-use 본 서한에 대한 회신으로 다음을 제출하라. • 에탄올 75%를 함유하는 것으로 표시된 위의 손소독제 의약품이 실제로는 평균 31%의 에탄올을 함유한 경위에 대한 상세한 조사. • 공급업체 이름, 주소, 연락처를 포함하여 귀사의 손소독제 의약품 제조에 사용된 모든 원료의 목록. • 귀사가 미국으로 선적한 모든 손소독제 의약품 배치의 목록과 유통한 모든 물량에 대한 전체 물량 대조(reconciliation). • 미국으로 유통된 모든 배치의 완전한 제조기록(batch record) 사본. 귀사 시설에서 제조된 것으로 표시된 손소독제 의약품의 함량 미달은 귀사 시설 내 품질보증이 Act 섹션 501(a)(2)(B)에 따른 CGMP 요건에 따라 기능하지 않음을 보여준다. 2 미승인 신약 및 허위표시 위반 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution은 질병의 진단, 치유, 완화, 치료 또는 예방에 사용할 의도이므로 FD&C Act 섹션 201(g)(1)(B), 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(B)에서 정의한 "의약품"에 해당하며, 및/또는 신체의 구조나 기능에 영향을 줄 의도이므로 FD&C Act 섹션 201(g)(1)(C), 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(C)에 따른 의약품에 해당한다. 구체적으로 이 제품은 외용 소독제(topical antiseptic)로 의도되었다. NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution의 제품 라벨 및 표시사항에서 관찰된 주장 중 이 제품의 의도된 용도(21 CFR 201.128에서 정의)를 입증하는 예는 다음을 포함하나 이에 국한되지 않는다. "HAND SANITIZER . . .. Drug Facts … Purpose …Antiseptic… Uses : Hand Sanitizer to help reduce bacteria that potentially can cause disease . . . Directions … Place enough product on hands to cover all surface. Rub hands together until dry." 이 외용 소독제 제품은 표시에 규정, 권장 또는 제시된 사용 조건에서 일반적으로 안전하고 유효하다고 인정되지(GRASE) 않으므로 FD&C Act 섹션 201(p), 21 U.S.C. 321(p)의 의미 내에서 "신약"이다. 신약은 FD&C Act 섹션 505G에 따라 합법적으로 판매되는 경우(아래에 추가로 설명하듯이 이 제품들에는 해당하지 않는다)를 제외하고는 FD&C Act 섹션 505(a), 21 U.S.C. 355(a)에 기술된 바와 같이 FDA의 사전 승인 없이 주 간 거래에 반입하거나 반입 목적으로 인도할 수 없다. 이 손소독제 제품에 대해서는 FD&C Act 섹션 505, 21 U.S.C. 355에 따른 FDA 승인 신청이 유효한 것이 없으며, 귀사의 "NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution" 의약품이 표시에 제시, 권장 또는 규정된 사용 조건에서 GRASE라는 판단을 뒷받침하는 적절하고 잘 통제된 임상시험도 공개 문헌에서 알지 못한다. 따라서 이 제품은 FD&C Act 섹션 505(a) 및 301(d), 21 U.S.C 355(a) 및 331(d)를 위반하여 판매된 미승인 신약이다. 일반의약품(OTC) 외용 소독제 제품은 FDA의 OTC Drug Review에 따른 규칙 제정의 대상이었음을 지적한다. 특히 이러한 제품은 "Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Tentative Final Monograph for Health-Care Antiseptic Drug Products," Proposed Rule, 59 FR 31402(1994년 6월 17일)(1994 TFM)라는 Tentative Final Monograph(TFM)에서 다루어졌으며, 이는 "Safety and Effectiveness of Consumer Antiseptics; Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Proposed Amendment of the Tentative Final Monograph; Reopening of Administrative Record," Proposed Rule, 81 FR 42912(2016년 6월 30일)(Consumer Antiseptic Rubs Proposed Rule)에 의해 추가로 개정되었다. 이러한 규칙 제정 과정에서 benzalkonium chloride, 에틸알코올(에탄올), 이소프로필알코올은 antiseptic rub용으로 Category III로 분류되었으며, 이는 이 유효성분 중 하나를 함유한 의약품이 소비자용 또는 의료인용 antiseptic rub으로 사용하기에 GRASE라는 판단을 뒷받침하려면 추가적인 안전성 및 유효성 데이터가 필요하다는 의미이다. FD&C Act 섹션 505G는 승인된 신청 없이 판매되는 일반의약품을 다룬다. FD&C Act 섹션 505G(a)(3)에 따라, 해당 의약품에 대해 21 CFR Part 330에 따라 발표된 가장 최근의 해당 제안 또는 판단인 TFM에서 안전성 또는 유효성에 대해 Category III로 분류되고 안전성 또는 유효성에 대해 Category II로 분류되지 않은 의약품은, 유효성분을 포함하여 해당 TFM에 개략된 관련 사용 조건에 부합하고 기타 모든 해당 요건을 준수하는 한 섹션 505에 따른 승인된 신청 없이 판매될 수 있다. 그러나 귀사의 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution 의약품은 2016년 Consumer Antiseptic Rub 제안 규칙에 의해 추가로 개정된 1994 TFM에도, 다른 어떤 TFM이나 최종 규칙에도 부합하지 않으며, 섹션 505에 따른 승인된 신청 없이 판매하기 위한 FD&C Act 섹션 505G(a)(3)의 조건을 충족하지 못한다. 제품 라벨에 따르면 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution 의약품은 유효성분 에틸알코올(에탄올) 75% v/v를 함유한다고 한다. 그러나 앞서 논의한 대로 국경에서 억류된 이 제품 한 배치에 대한 FDA 실험실 분석은 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution이 제품 라벨에 기재된 75% v/v보다 낮고 1994 TFM 3 에 기술된 에탄올 양보다도 낮은 농도의 에탄올을 함유함을 입증했다. 이러한 제품은 TFM이나 해당 요건에 부합하지 않으며, COVID-19 공중보건 비상사태 중 손소독제에 대한 FDA의 임시 정책을 제시한 가이던스에 기술된 제제와도 일치하지 않는다. 4 또한 이 손소독제는 표시가 허위이거나 오인 소지가 있으므로 FD&C Act 섹션 502(a), 21 U.S.C. 352(a)에 따라 허위표시 의약품이다. 위에서 언급한 대로 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution은 에탄올 75% v/v를 함유하는 것으로 표시되어 있다. 그러나 이 제품에 대한 FDA 실험실 분석은 제품이 제품 라벨에 기재된 것보다 훨씬 낮은 농도의 에탄올을 함유함을 보여준다. 따라서 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution 표시사항의 유효성분 에탄올 농도에 대한 오인 소지가 있는 표현은 이 제품을 FD&C Act 섹션 502(a), 21 U.S.C. 352(a)에 따른 허위표시 의약품으로 만든다. 마지막으로 이 제품은 NATURAL GOLD GEL ALCOHOL ANTISEPTIC 75% Topical Solution이 FD&C Act 섹션 505G, 21 U.S.C. 355h의 적용을 받는 일반의약품이지만 해당 섹션에 따른 판매 요건을 준수하지 않고 FD&C Act 섹션 505, 21 U.S.C. 355에 따라 승인된 신청의 대상도 아니므로 FD&C Act 섹션 502(ee), 21 U.S.C. 352(ee)에 따른 허위표시 의약품이다. 허위표시 의약품을 주 간 거래에 반입하거나 반입 목적으로 인도하는 행위는 FD&C Act 섹션 301(a), 21 U.S.C. 331(a)에 의해 금지된다. CGMP 컨설턴트 권고 귀사에서 확인된 위반의 성격에 비추어, 귀사가 미국 시장용 의약품 제조를 재개하려는 경우 21 CFR 211.34에 규정된 자격을 갖춘 컨설턴트를 고용하여 귀사의 운영을 평가하고 귀사가 CGMP 요건을 충족하도록 지원받을 것을 강력히 권고한다. 또한 자격을 갖춘 컨설턴트가 귀사 전체 운영의 CGMP 준수에 대한 포괄적인 감사를 수행하고, 귀사가 FDA와의 준수 상태 해결을 추진하기 전에 시정 및 예방 조치(CAPA)의 완료와 효과성을 평가할 것을 권고한다. 컨설턴트를 이용한다고 해서 귀사의 CGMP 준수 의무가 면제되지는 않는다. 귀사 경영진은 지속적인 CGMP 준수를 보장하기 위해 모든 결함과 시스템상의 결함을 해결할 책임이 있다.

finding_text: This letter concerns your firm’s distribution of over-the-counter (OTC) stimulant drug products. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has reviewed your website, (https://wardsmellingsalts.com/) and your social media account on Facebook, where your ”BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” drug products are available for purchase in the United States. Based on our review, your ”BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” drug products are unapproved new drugs introduced or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce in violation of section 505(a) of the Federal Food Drug & Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 355(a), and are misbranded under section 502(ee) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(ee). Introduction or delivery for introduction of such products into interstate commerce is prohibited under sections 301(d) and (a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d) and (a). These violations are described in more detail below. Unapproved New Drug and Misbranded Drug Violations ”BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” are drugs as defined by section 201(g)(1)(B) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(B), because they are intended for use in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease and/or under section 201(g)(1)(C) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(C), because they are intended to affect the structure or any function of the body. Specifically, these products are intended for use as stimulant drug products. Examples of the claims from the products’ labeling, including your products’ labels and website and your social media accounts on Facebook and Instagram, that provide evidence of the intended uses (as defined in 21 CFR 201.128) of the products include, but may not be limited to, the following: BOTTLED INSANITY XL “Smelling Salts…Energy…Focus…Strength…Ingredients: Sodium Carbonate, Ammonium Chloride…Uncap, Sniff, Perform” [from your product label] ”Insane Smelling Salts…Smelling salts, also known as 'ammonia inhalants' are used by athletes for a sudden adrenaline rush that allows them to perform like never before. Our insane formula unlocks your full potential. Uncap, sniff, perform,” “They're becoming hugely popular in any sport that requires short and powerful bursts of energy…” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/] ”Our insanely powerful smelling salts allow athletes like yourself to push their training and performance to a whole new level.” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/pages/about-us] ”Smelling salts work by causing a sudden release of adrenaline that allows you to push your athletic performance beyond anything you've experienced….Uncap, sniff, perform….Sniff directly from the bottle to get a powerful adrenaline rush from ward’s most insane ammonia inhalant formula” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/products/bottled-insanity-insane-smelling-salt] “What are smelling salts/ammonia inhalants?...smelling salts are used by athletes for sudden rushes of adrenaline.” [from your Facebook social media account https://www.facebook.com/WardSmellingSalts/] “Sniff directly from the bottle to get a powerful adrenaline rush from ward’s most insane ammonia inhalant formula” [from your Instagram social media account https://www.instagram.com/p/CLr-iJVAdbw/] HOCKEY SMELLING SALT “Smelling Salt…Ammonia Inhalant…Uncap, Sniff, Perform” [from your product label] ”Insane Smelling Salts…Smelling salts, also known as 'ammonia inhalants' are used by athletes for a sudden adrenaline rush that allows them to perform like never before. Our insane formula unlocks your full potential. Uncap, sniff, perform,” “They're becoming hugely popular in any sport that requires short and powerful bursts of energy…” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/] ”Our insanely powerful smelling salts allow athletes like yourself to push their training and performance to a whole new level.” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/pages/about-us] ”Smelling salts work by causing a sudden release of adrenaline that allows you to push your athletic performance beyond anything you've experienced….Skate Faster, shoot harder, win more games!” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/products/hockey-smelling-salts-formulated-for-cold-conditions] “What are smelling salts/ammonia inhalants?...smelling salts are used by athletes for sudden rushes of adrenaline.” [from your Facebook social media account https://www.facebook.com/WardSmellingSalts/] ASYLUM REFILL PACK “Uncap, Sniff, Perform…Ammonia Inhalant…Ingredients: Sodium Carbonate, Ammonium Chloride” [from your product label] ”Insane Smelling Salts…Smelling salts, also known as 'ammonia inhalants' are used by athletes for a sudden adrenaline rush that allows them to perform like never before. Our insane formula unlocks your full potential. Uncap, sniff, perform,” “They're becoming hugely popular in any sport that requires short and powerful bursts of energy…” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/] ”Our insanely powerful smelling salts allow athletes like yourself to push their training and performance to a whole new level.” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/pages/about-us] ”Outperform yourself…Unleash your true athletic potential with our insanely powerful smelling salt formula.” [from your products’ website https://wardsmellingsalts.com/products/asylum-refill-pack-smelling-salt] “What are smelling salts/ammonia inhalants?...smelling salts are used by athletes for sudden rushes of adrenaline.” [from your Facebook social media account https://www.facebook.com/WardSmellingSalts/] Based on the above labeling claims, “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” drug products, , are intended for use as stimulant drug products. Specifically, these products are intended for use as both reflex stimulants (i.e., smelling salts, ammonia inhalants) and, more generally, as stimulants to help restore mental alertness or wakefulness. As described below, these stimulant drug products are unapproved new drugs marketed in violation of sections 505(a) and 301(d) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C 355(a) and 331(d). In general, a drug product is a “new drug” within the meaning of section 201(p) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 321(p), if it is not generally recognized as safe and effective (GRASE) for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in its labeling; and in general, new drugs may not be introduced or delivered for introduction into interstate commerce without an approved application from FDA in effect, as described in section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355(a). No FDA-approved applications pursuant to section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355, are in effect for the products identified above. “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” are reflex stimulant drug products subject to section 505G of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355h, which governs nonprescription drugs marketed without an approved application. Specifically, these reflex stimulant drug products are deemed to be new drugs under section 505G(a)(4) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355h(a)(4), because they are subject to a determination to be not GRASE in a proposed rule that is the most recently applicable proposal issued under 21 CFR part 330. The term “smelling salt” typically is used to refer to an ammonia aromatic preparation used as a reflex stimulant. 1 On June 19, 2008, FDA issued a proposed rule (73 FR 34895) 2 setting forth a determination that ammonia and any other ammonia ingredient 3 in a drug product that is labeled with claims or directions for use as a reflex stimulant are not GRASE or are misbranded. This June 19, 2008 proposed rule is the most recent applicable FDA proposal issued under 21 CFR part 330 with respect to ammonia as a reflex stimulant in OTC drug products. Thus, “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” are deemed to be new drugs under section 201(p)(1) of the FD&C Act and subject to the requirement to have an approved new drug application under section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355, beginning on September 23, 2020. 4 Even if “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” were not marketed as reflex stimulant drug products and were only marketed as more general stimulant drug products, your products would still not meet the requirements under section 505G, under which they would be deemed to be GRASE and not a new drug. Under section 505G of the FD&C Act, certain nonprescription drugs marketed without an approved application —commonly referred to as "OTC monograph drugs"—may be legally marketed if they meet applicable requirements. In particular, nonprescription stimulant drug products are deemed to be GRASE and not a “new drug” if, among other things, they conform to the conditions of use in the Over-the-Counter Monograph, M011: Stimulant Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use (hereinafter M011), as set forth in the applicable final administrative order. 5 However, your “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” stimulant drug products do not conform to the conditions of use specified in Monograph M011 because, per the labeling of your products, they are not formulatedwith caffeine, which is the only permitted active ingredient in Monograph M011, and are labeled with directions for intranasal administration, neither of which are covered under the deemed final order. 6 Therefore, even if “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” were marketed only as general stimulant drug products, they would not meet requirements under section 505G, under which they would be deemed to be GRASE and not new drugs. In addition, FDA is not aware of any adequate and well-controlled clinical trials in the published literature that support a determination that “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” are GRASE for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in their labeling. Moreover, there is no evident basis under the FD&C Act under which these products would be legally marketed without an approved application. Accordingly, these products are unapproved new drugs marketed in violation of section 505(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C 355(a). Introduction or delivery for introduction of such products into interstate commerce is prohibited under section 301(d) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d). Lastly, “BOTTLED INSANITY XL,” “HOCKEY SMELLING SALT,” and “ASYLUM REFILL PACK” are misbranded under section 502(ee) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(ee), because they are nonprescription drugs subject to section 505G of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355h, but do not comply with the requirements for marketing under that section and are not the subjects of applications approved under section 505 of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 355. The introduction or delivery for introduction of a misbranded drug into interstate commerce is prohibited under section 301(a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(a).
finding_text_ko: 이 서한은 일반의약품(OTC) 각성제(stimulant) 의약품의 귀사 유통과 관련된다. 미국 식품의약국(FDA)은 귀사의 웹사이트(https://wardsmellingsalts.com/)와 Facebook 소셜 미디어 계정을 검토했으며, 여기서 귀사의 "BOTTLED INSANITY XL," "HOCKEY SMELLING SALT," "ASYLUM REFILL PACK" 의약품이 미국에서 구매 가능하다. 검토 결과 귀사의 "BOTTLED INSANITY XL," "HOCKEY SMELLING SALT," "ASYLUM REFILL PACK" 의약품은 연방식품의약품화장품법(FD&C Act) 섹션 505(a), 21 U.S.C. 355(a)를 위반하여 주 간(interstate) 거래에 반입되거나 반입 목적으로 인도된 미승인 신약이며 FD&C Act 섹션 502(ee), 21 U.S.C. 352(ee)에 따른 허위표시(misbranded) 의약품이다. 이러한 제품을 주 간 거래에 반입하거나 반입 목적으로 인도하는 행위는 FD&C Act 섹션 301(d) 및 (a), 21 U.S.C. 331(d) 및 (a)에 의해 금지된다. 이 위반 사항은 아래에 더 자세히 설명한다. 미승인 신약 및 허위표시 의약품 위반 "BOTTLED INSANITY XL," "HOCKEY SMELLING SALT," "ASYLUM REFILL PACK"은 질병의 진단, 치유, 완화, 치료 또는 예방에 사용할 의도이므로 FD&C Act 섹션 201(g)(1)(B), 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(B)에서 정의한 의약품에 해당하며, 및/또는 신체의 구조나 기능에 영향을 줄 의도이므로 FD&C Act 섹션 201(g)(1)(C), 21 U.S.C. 321(g)(1)(C)에 따른 의약품에 해당한다. 구체적으로 이 제품들은 각성제 의약품으로 사용할 의도이다. 귀사 제품의 라벨과 웹사이트, Facebook 및 Instagram 소셜 미디어 계정을 포함한 제품 표시사항에서, 이 제품들의 의도된 용도(21 CFR 201.128에서 정의)를 입증하는 주장의 예는 다음을 포함하나 이에 국한되지 않는다.
